T: They're coming to get you, Barbara.
D: Strangers barricade themselves in a farmhouse as the dead rise.
P: Serve the snacks when everyone boards up the windows.
S: whatever's in the cupboard while the boards go up

Saltine crackers piled with tinned sardines mashed with lemon and parsley, sharp cheddar, and a quick pickled red onion, laid out on a chopping board. Thinly slice 1 red onion and soak it in 80ml white vinegar with 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes. Drain 2 x 110g tins sardines and mash lightly with the juice of half a lemon, chopped parsley and pepper. Slice 150g sharp cheddar. Top 24 saltine crackers with sardine, a slice of cheddar and a few pickled onion rings and lay them out on a chopping board.
Barbara and Johnny's visit to their father's grave
Egg and cress, and ham and mustard on buttered white bread, crusts off, wrapped in wax paper like a 1968 picnic.
Popcorn tossed half in melted butter and fine salt, half in butter, cracked black pepper and black sesame.
M: cooked on the stove while the windows get boarded
Beef chuck browned, onion, carrot and potato, stock and thyme, braised covered at 160C for 2.5 hours. Crusty bread.
Ben's beef and bean chilli with cornbread
Ben pulls up at the farmhouse in a truck

Beef mince chilli simmered with cumin, chilli and kidney beans, ladled into bowls over sour cream and cheddar, with hot buttered cornbread on the side. Brown 700g beef mince in batches. Cook 1 diced onion and 3 garlic cloves 5 minutes, add 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp smoked paprika, then 2 x 400g tins tomatoes and 400g drained kidney beans. Simmer 45 minutes. Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 300ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter, pour into a hot buttered pan and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Serve with sour cream and cheddar.
W: what's left in the farmhouse pantry

Tinned peach halves baked under a golden cinnamon biscuit topping until bubbling, served warm with a jug of cold pouring cream. Drain 2 x 825g tins peach halves, keeping 100ml syrup. Toss the peaches with the syrup and 1 tbsp cornflour in a baking dish. Rub 80g cold butter into 200g self-raising flour, 60g caster sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, then mix in 120ml milk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake at 190C for 30 minutes until golden. Serve warm with 300ml pouring cream.
K: the long night boarded up in the farmhouse

Strong stovetop coffee sweetened with brown sugar and a nip of Irish whiskey, topped with lightly whipped cream so it floats. Brew 800ml strong coffee in a stovetop pot or plunger. Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out. Put 2 tsp brown sugar and 30ml Irish whiskey in each glass, pour in 200ml hot coffee and stir to dissolve. Whip 150ml thickened cream until just thick enough to pour, then float it over the back of a spoon. Skip the whiskey for anyone who wants it plain.

s.note: Egg and cress, ham and mustard on buttered white bread.
s.how: Boil 2 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and mash with 20g mayonnaise. Stir in 10g chopped cress. Butter 8 slices white bread with 25g softened butter. Use four slices to make two egg-and-cress sandwiches. Use the other four for two sandwiches with 80g leg ham and 10g Dijon mustard. Trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into four small pieces. Wrap in wax paper for a 1968-style picnic and serve four pieces each.

s.note: Buttered popcorn, half salted and half with pepper and black sesame.
s.how: Pop 60g popcorn kernels in 1 tbsp neutral oil in a covered pot over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking regularly. Divide equally. Toss one half with 15g melted butter and 1/4 tsp fine salt. Toss the other with 15g melted butter, 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper and 10g black sesame seeds. Arrange side by side in a shared bowl.

m.note: Slow braised beef with onion, carrot, potato, thyme and crusty bread.
m.how: Cut 800g beef chuck into chunks and season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Brown in 1 tbsp neutral oil in a heavy casserole for 8 minutes, in batches. Add 1 chopped brown onion, 2 chopped carrots, 500g potato chunks, 500ml beef stock and 4 thyme sprigs. Cover and braise at 160°C conventional for 2.5 hours, stirring once, until the beef is tender. Serve with 200g crusty Italian bread for soaking up the stock.
